title: Item 1's Files section never rewires the actual write call sites for 3 of its 8 named tables (ipo_details, financial_statements, ipo_valuation) — they keep writing through the old, non-consolidated path
detail: Item 1's Purpose and Schema sections claim all eight tables — 'ipo_details, financial_statements, ipo_valuation, ipo_risk_factors, promoters, anchor_investors, ipo_intermediaries, peer_companies' — get 'per-field priority resolution, field_sources rows, and data_conflicts detection'. But the card's Files table only names call-site changes for the five whole-row-replace tables: 'The five replaceAllowed(...) call sites for whole-row replace (promoters line 1390, promoter_acquisition_ranges line 1435, ipo_risk_factors line 1518, ipo_intermediaries line 1644, peer_companies line 1701)... are replaced by calls to orchestrator.consolidatedUpsertChildRows', plus anchor-persister.ts:540-541. It never names a change to the ipo_details, financial_statements, or ipo_valuation write sites. I read those three sites in scraper/src/services/filing-persister.ts (this session, current main): ipo_details is written via `await deps.ipoDetailsWriter.upsert(ipoId, {...detailsWritable, dataSource: source})` followed by a bare `await trackField('ipo_details', col)` per column (~line 991-996); financial_statements via `await deps.financialStatements.upsert({ipoId, fiscalYear, basis, ...})` followed by `await trackField('financial_statements', 'rows')` (~line 1250-1273); ipo_valuation via `await deps.ipoValuation.upsert({ipoId, pricingEvent, ...})` followed by `await trackField('ipo_valuation', pricingEvent)` (~line 1315-1355). `trackField` is a bare provenance stamp with no priority resolution and no conflict detection — a completely different, third write pattern from the five the card actually rewires. Item 1's own worked example even calls `consolidatedUpsertChildRows(ipoId, 'financial_statements', ...)` as if this were already wired, but no line in the Files table tells an implementer to replace the real call at filing-persister.ts's financial_statements/ipo_valuation/ipo_details sites with that call. An implementer following the Files table literally ships the schema migration and the five replace-based rewires, runs the listed unit/integration tests (which exercise the interface directly, not filing-persister.ts's real call sites), and reports done — while revenue, EBITDA, EPS, valuation multiples and every ipo_details field keep flowing through the old no-priority-resolution path. This directly recreates, for 3 of 8 tables, the exact gap §7.1 says item 1 exists to close ('208 of 240 fields have no consolidated writer at all... the pull loop would have nowhere to put 87% of what it extracts'), and starves item 5/6's field_sources-driven walk of real provenance for financial and valuation data specifically.
where: docs/design/build-cards/item-01-child-table-consolidated-writer.md — 'Files' table (rows for data-consolidation-orchestrator.ts and filing-persister.ts) and the 'Worked example' under Interfaces; contradicted by scraper/src/services/filing-persister.ts:991-1005 (ipo_details), :1250-1273 (financial_statements), :1315-1355 (ipo_valuation)
recommendation: Add three explicit Files rows naming the ipo_details/financial_statements/ipo_valuation call sites in filing-persister.ts, replacing `deps.ipoDetailsWriter.upsert`/`deps.financialStatements.upsert`/`deps.ipoValuation.upsert` + their bare `trackField` calls with `orchestrator.consolidatedUpsertChildRows(ipoId, tableName, [row], source, docType)`, and add a unit test asserting filing-persister.ts calls the orchestrator (not the raw repository) for these three tables, mirroring the promoters/risk_factors tests already specified.

title: Item 1 adds three new UNIQUE constraints to production tables with no pre-migration duplicate check or repair step
detail: Item 1's Schema section requires adding brand-new unique constraints to tables that have NEVER had one: `promoters` gets `(ipoId, normalizedName)` ('The table has no unique constraint today... because the current write path deletes every row and reinserts'), `ipo_intermediaries` gets `(ipoId, role, normalizedName)` ('none exists today because the write path is whole-table replace'), and `peer_companies` gets `(ipoId, normalizedName)` ('No unique constraint today... same replace-then-insert reason as promoters'). The card's migration section shows the field_sources/data_conflicts row_key migration in full but gives no equivalent DDL, pre-flight duplicate-scan query, or repair tool for these three NEW constraints on promoters/ipo_intermediaries/peer_companies. Because these tables were written by delete-then-insert with no identity concept until now, nothing in the current or historical write path ever prevented two rows normalizing to the same key within a single replace batch (e.g. a promoter and a group-entity of the same name both parsed from one document, or a peer company listed under two share classes) — the risk is exactly the kind the card itself names as real ('a mainboard IPO commonly has 2-4 BRLMs and several syndicate members under the same role value' is given as the reason role-alone collides, i.e. real documents already produce near-duplicate name+role combinations). Running `ALTER TABLE promoters ADD CONSTRAINT ... UNIQUE (ipo_id, normalized_name)` against a table with even one existing duplicate pair fails outright and blocks the whole migration (which also carries the field_sources/data_conflicts row_key changes item 5 and item 6 depend on), with no rollback-safe path described.
where: docs/design/build-cards/item-01-child-table-consolidated-writer.md — 'Schema' table rows for promoters, ipo_intermediaries, peer_companies ('Requires adding a unique constraint...')
recommendation: Before generating the migration, run a duplicate-scan query per table (`GROUP BY ipo_id, normalized_name HAVING count(*) > 1` for promoters/peer_companies; `GROUP BY ipo_id, role, normalized_name HAVING count(*) > 1` for ipo_intermediaries) against staging and prod, and add a repair step (keep newest by updated_at, or merge) to the card before the ADD CONSTRAINT statement — or gate the constraint addition behind a script that repairs-then-migrates in one deploy, the same pattern item 11 already uses for its own repair tool.

title: The §7.1 'Depends on' column for item 6 lists only item 5, omitting item 15 — which item 6's own card names as a hard prerequisite
detail: §7.1's sequence table row for item 6 reads: '6 | The pull walk over the plan | 5 | A | large — the core'. That is the only dependency edge a reader of the table sees. But item 6's own build card states, twice, that item 15 is a real prerequisite, not merely related work: in Serves — 'the explicit prerequisite named in §2.5.2: item 15 (valueActuallyChanged) must land first or the walk's own no-op-suppression cannot be verified' — and in its Detection section, discussing check PULL-NOOP: 'This check is unbuildable-as-meaningful without item 15... Item 6 does not fix item 15; it depends on it.' Item 6's own 'Tier, budget and cost' section even flags the table gap itself: 'this card's own dependency on item 15 (not listed as a direct §7.1 dependency edge...) means a reviewer should confirm item 15 has actually landed... before approving this item's merge.' Despite the card being self-aware, the SSOT sequencing table that a scheduler or a second implementer would consult first (§7.1, not every card's prose) still only shows '5' in item 6's Depends-on cell. A build ordered strictly off that table's dependency column can start item 6 the moment item 5 lands, without item 15 — shipping a PULL-NOOP check that (per the card's own words) 'would read every higher-priority-source re-confirmation as a real write... never go green on a quiet day even when the walk is behaving correctly', which is precisely the class of drift F-49 already found and that item 6 exists partly to close.
where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §7.1 sequence table, row 6 ('Depends on' column reads '5'); contradicted by docs/design/build-cards/item-06-pull-walk.md 'Serves', 'Detection', and 'Tier, budget and cost' sections
recommendation: Update §7.1's item-6 'Depends on' cell to '5, 15' so the table itself — not just item 6's prose — carries the real dependency, and add a one-line note under the table (as items 7/17 already get) explaining why 15 is listed even though it is not a schema/code prerequisite in the strict sense, only a verification one.

title: Item 7 schedules GMP inside the market-hours-gated live-figures job (10:00-18:30 IST), which reverts the owner-approved fix for F-41 (GMP staleness up to ~65h over a weekend) without resolving the contradiction
detail: F-41 in findings.json is status FIXED: 'GMP is gated to market hours with subscription, so it is stale exactly when people read it... Up to ~65h stale over a weekend. Proposed: split the live step — subscription and demand graph stay gated, GMP runs every wake while UPCOMING or OPEN.' closed_in: 'owner approved 2026-09-08: split the live step, GMP runs every wake while UPCOMING or OPEN' — i.e. GMP was explicitly taken OUT of the market-hours gate one day before OD-19. Item 7's own card puts GMP back inside the gate: '§2.1's job table puts GMP (grey-market premium) inside the live-figures job, gated to 10:00-18:30 IST and to days with an OPEN IPO — the same market-hours gate that finding F-41... explicitly removed GMP from, because GMP is most active exactly when this gate is closed (evenings, weekends).' The card names this as an 'Open contradiction surfaced, not resolved here' and proceeds anyway 'because that is the literal text under "What runs, and when"' in OD-19, while recommending the owner confirm in one line before shipping. As written, and absent that owner confirmation being captured anywhere in the design or findings.json, building item 7 to the letter of its own PM2/cron table (`*/30 10-18 * * * scripts/scraper-wake.sh live` carrying GMP) re-introduces a measured, user-visible data-staleness regression on a field the design itself calls the single highest-signal number retail investors read, on every evening and every weekend, going forward — this is not a hypothetical edge case, it is the exact scenario F-41 measured and fixed.
where: docs/design/build-cards/item-07-job-scheduler-and-budgets.md — 'Purpose'/'Open contradiction surfaced, not resolved here' paragraph and the PM2 cron table under 'Interfaces'; docs/design/findings.json F-41 (status FIXED, closed_in note)
recommendation: Do not merge item 7 until the owner has explicitly answered, in writing (a line in findings.json or §2.1), whether OD-19 supersedes F-41's fix for GMP specifically. If OD-19 does not intend to supersede F-41, split GMP out of the live-figures cron line into its own ungated 'every wake while UPCOMING or OPEN' entry, exactly as F-41's closure describes, and update the PM2 table accordingly before this card is built.

title: web/lib/utils/rating-calculator.ts has the identical dormant-threshold-activation defect as ipo-scoring-realtime.ts (tracked as F-95), but item 11 documents it without adding it to the fix scope, tests, or detection
detail: The task brief's known-findings list records F-95 as 'the crore conversion activates a dormant scoring bug in ipo-scoring-realtime.ts' — one file. Item 11's own Files table, however, independently documents a second file with the same defect class: 'web/lib/utils/rating-calculator.ts:164-168 — Same pattern, same thresholds (>= 1000, >= 500, < 100), same currently-dormant behaviour, same activation risk' as ipo-scoring-realtime.ts's calculateFundamentals() (which the card describes in the row immediately above: 'compares Number(ipo.issueSize) against 1000/500/100 — thresholds that only make sense in crore. Today... every row is > 1000 and this component is a silent always-max no-op. The crore conversion activates this scoring component for the first time in production... Call this out to QA/PM explicitly; it is not covered by this item's own tests'). That explicit 'call this out, not covered by tests' instruction is written for ipo-scoring-realtime.ts only — the rating-calculator.ts row carries no equivalent instruction, no test reference, and is absent from the card's Tests and Detection sections entirely. An implementer or reviewer scoping this item off F-95's single-file framing (the only place this class is tracked with an id) will fix/flag ipo-scoring-realtime.ts and silently leave rating-calculator.ts's rating output wrong for every IPO the day the conversion ships — a second silent always-extreme-score defect activated by the same release, undetected by the same gap.
where: docs/design/build-cards/item-11-crore-conversion.md — 'Files' table, the two consecutive rows for web/lib/services/ipo-scoring-realtime.ts:390-396 and web/lib/utils/rating-calculator.ts:164-168
recommendation: Extend F-95's tracked fix scope (or open a companion finding) to explicitly name rating-calculator.ts, add the identical 'call this out to QA/PM, recalibrate or gate the thresholds' instruction item 11 already gives ipo-scoring-realtime.ts, and add both files to the same test/detection coverage before this item ships.

title: field_extraction_failures.rowKey is defined nullable with a 'null for singleton tables' comment, contradicting item 1's explicit non-null '' convention for the same key — breaking the join item 4's own comment promises
detail: Item 1's Schema section is emphatic and specific about row_key's nullability, twice: 'Never null — a nullable column can't sit inside a unique constraint the way an empty string can (two NULLs are not equal under a unique index; two '' are), which is exactly why '' is the singleton sentinel, not null' — and defines it as `rowKey: varchar('row_key', { length: 200 }).notNull().default('')`. Item 5's ipo_field_plan repeats the identical convention verbatim for the same reason. Item 4's Schema, however, defines field_extraction_failures.rowKey as `varchar('row_key', { length: 100 })` — no `.notNull()`, no `.default('')` — with a comment reading 'Item 1's row_key (null for ipos and every singleton child table; populated for financial_statements/promoters/anchor_investors/etc. rows, matching field_sources.row_key exactly so the two tables join)'. That comment both misstates item 1's own rule (item 1 uses '' for singletons, never null) and then claims a join guarantee ('matching field_sources.row_key exactly') that the chosen nullability breaks: in SQL, `NULL = ''` evaluates to NULL/false, so a JOIN or WHERE clause correlating field_extraction_failures.rowKey with field_sources.rowKey or ipo_field_plan.rowKey on a singleton-table row (ipos, ipo_details, anchor_investors, financial_data) will never match, silently losing exactly the cross-table correlation ('which document said this failed, and what does its provenance record show') that item 4's own comment says this column exists for. The column is also declared varchar(100) here versus varchar(200) in item 1/item 5, a second, smaller inconsistency in the same field.
where: docs/design/build-cards/item-04-per-field-validation.md — 'Schema' section, `fieldExtractionFailures` table, `rowKey` column and its comment; contradicted by docs/design/build-cards/item-01-child-table-consolidated-writer.md 'Schema' section's rowKey definition and rationale, and docs/design/build-cards/item-05-ipo-field-plan-table.md's identical rowKey definition
recommendation: Change field_extraction_failures.rowKey to `varchar('row_key', { length: 200 }).notNull().default('')`, matching item 1/item 5 exactly, and correct the comment to say '\'\' for ipos and every singleton child table' rather than 'null'. Add a unit test asserting a join between field_extraction_failures and field_sources on (ipoId, tableName, rowKey, fieldName) actually returns rows for a singleton-table failure, since this is precisely the case the current definition would silently fail.
